solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inherited icon — mate devastated

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked, so the letters of the two words are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A treasured icon has been smashed by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastated' shuffles ICON and MATE into the two words of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money or property is the idiom for receiving it as an inheritance.

clue.text: Doctor wearing outer garment, sort of jacket

indicators.note: wearing says the doctor is inside the garment

parts.note: a coat is an outer garment
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor in an overcoat, some kind of jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the surface, but it supplies a medical degree abbreviation; 'wearing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A military-style field jacket is known by this word, as in the combat jacket.

clue.text: A wit badly described by brand new US novelist

indicators.note: described by means drawn around, so the outer letters surround the scrambled ones

parts.note: a brand is a mark

indicators.note: badly says the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A clumsy joke is told about a fresh American writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' means drawn round, the geometry sense of describe, so it signals a container; 'badly' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Clemens wrote under this pen name; he was the author of Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Tina — she changed hurriedly

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Tina got dressed in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with haste means doing it quickly or hurriedly.

clue.text: A test involved a small sample only

indicators.note: involved suggests twisted together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Only a small number of people took part in the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste is just a little bit of something tried, a small sample.

clue.text: Scallywag, one providing seafood

parts.note: a scallywag is a scamp, a mischievous rascal
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A rascal is selling fish on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails served as a dish are a familiar seafood item.

clue.text: Solve first of conundrums humorist raised

indicators.note: first of says take the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Edward Lear was a humorist, the writer of nonsense verse
raised means up

explanation.surface: Work out the opening puzzle a comic writer has posed.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear was the English writer of nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussycat.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a mystery is to solve it, an everyday idiom.

clue.text: I am to be found in Michigan tourist centre

indicators.note: to be found in says the words are placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says they are in Michigan visiting the sights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be found in' is the container signal; the state is reduced to its two-letter postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami in Florida is a major holiday destination and tourist centre.

clue.text: Attempt to follow Asian river craft

indicators.note: to follow says the attempt comes after the river

parts.note: the Indus is a river in Asia, flowing through Pakistan
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Trying to trace an Asian river by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft can mean skilled work or a trade, which is a sense of industry.

clue.text: Nursing home's senior nurse left

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the nurse word holds the home word

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals
in means at home

explanation.surface: A nursing home's chief nurse has gone away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing' signals a container: one piece holds the other. In Britain a sister is a senior ward nurse, and left in heraldry is sinister.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is the heraldic and Latin term for the left-hand side.

clue.text: Girl, very sad in stormy Massachusetts resort

parts.note: Martha is a girl's name

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters of the three words are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl is gloomy while the weather is rough at a seaside holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' is the anagram signal for the three words after the girl's name; the Massachusetts island is spelt with an apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: This island off Cape Cod is a well-known summer holiday destination in that state.

clue.text: Cunning is the heartless entertainer

parts.note: art can mean cunning or craftiness

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letter of the word 'the' is taken away

explanation.surface: A crafty and unfeeling performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes H, the central letter of THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer, especially a singer or dancer, is called by this French-derived word.

clue.text: Dilapidated pub, cut off, is run poorly

indicators.note: cut off says the last letter of the pub word is lopped

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: poorly suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rundown pub that has been isolated is badly managed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' trims INN to IN; 'poorly' rearranges IS RUN to RUINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that has fallen into ruin is in a dilapidated, broken-down state.

clue.text: Head girl originally defines a filbert

parts.note: Hazel is a girl's name
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A school's head girl explains what a filbert is.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a school head girl; split it into 'Head' and 'girl', which join in the reverse of their clue order, a swap 'originally' only loosely hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: The filbert is another name for the cultivated cobnut grown on hazel trees.

clue.text: A bulletin was sent out about Charlie

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go around the extra letter
out suggests the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A news report was issued concerning someone called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container signal; Charlie stands for its letter in the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio or television news broadcast is a type of bulletin.

clue.text: The fire-raiser's game?

parts.note: the iron rod used to stir up a fire is called by the same name as a card game played for stakes

explanation.definitionFit: The fireside iron used to rouse flames shares its name with the card game.

clue.text: Animal in a lake — boar, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A wild pig might be swimming in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian marsupial that eats eucalyptus is a familiar animal.

clue.text: Fictitious place in book about redistribution of tin

indicators.note: about says the book word goes around the shuffled metal

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: redistribution means sharing out differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A book discusses how a metal is reallocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redistribution of' is the anagram signal and 'about' puts the book around the result; Atlantis was Plato's lost island.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato described this sunken island kingdom, a legendary and imaginary place.

clue.text: Units destroyed in African capital

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters of the word are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Military units were wiped out in an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia in North Africa.

clue.text: Romans wandering around centre of new Italian resort

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the central letter
wandering suggests straying, so the letters are moved around
centre of says take the middle letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Romans touring a new seaside town in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges ROMANS to SANRMO, and 'around' puts it round E, the centre of NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: This Ligurian coastal town is a famous resort on the Italian Riviera.

clue.text: Clever repartee in fencing? Not with son

indicators.note: not with says the son's letter is to be left out of the fencing word

parts.note: fencing is swordplay

explanation.surface: Witty banter during a fencing bout, though not with the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Witty play on words, puns and quips, is a form of clever verbal repartee.

clue.text: Find fault with a revolutionary's grand manner

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
Che Guevara was a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Criticising a rebel's showy style.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant confidence and style, a dashing flair, is a grand manner.

clue.text: Cause resentment in joint after start of rehearsal

indicators.note: after says the joint comes after the opening letter
start of says take the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an ankle is a joint

explanation.surface: An actor nurses a sore joint after a rehearsal, feeling bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: When a slight lingers and causes bitterness, it is said to fester and annoy.

clue.text: As found in vaccines radiographer brought back

indicators.note: brought back says the hidden letters are read backwards
found in says the letters are concealed within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Vials of vaccine handed back by a hospital radiographer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'As found' as the definition, but 'found in' is the hiding signal and 'As' alone defines, being the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol of this poisonous element, number 33 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Musical instrument, one carried by celebrity

indicators.note: carried by says the one sits inside the celebrity word

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A famous person carries a guitar-like instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked Indian lute is a stringed musical instrument.

clue.text: In Vermont, an American state

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Vermont, an American state is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Montana is one of the fifty United States, lying in the north-west of the country.

clue.text: Girl's tropical fish

definitions.meaning: A girl's name; the 's stands for 'is'
a small livebearing aquarium fish from warm American waters

explanation.definitionFit: It is a pet form of Mary and also a small freshwater aquarium fish.

clue.text: A patterned cloth in torn shreds? All agree

parts.note: tatters are torn shreds of cloth
taken as written
to check is to agree or tally, as figures that check

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees a piece of fabric is in rags.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a British fabric design of coloured lines forming squares on a light ground, named after Tattersalls horse market.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woven fabric with a pattern of crossing coloured stripes forming squares.

clue.text: Address Poles about more suffering

indicators.note: about says the polar letters go around the scrambled word

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles

indicators.note: suffering suggests something distressed, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Polish people talk about further hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not Polish people but the two compass poles; 'suffering' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk or address, especially one given from a pulpit, is this.

clue.text: Exclamation of pop star dropping ring

indicators.note: dropping says the ring letter falls out of the star's name

parts.note: Boy George is the singer of Culture Club
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A pop singer loses a ring and cries out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes an O from BOY GEORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned oath of surprise, invoking a saint's name, is an exclamation.
